title: Proper direct-image bound for arbitrary torsion etale sheaves
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $d\geq0$ be an integer, and assume that for every $y\in Y$ the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $d$. Empty fibres have dimension $-\infty$. For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on the small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], the higher direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] satisfy $$R^qf_*F=0\qquad(q>2d).$$ No quasi-compactness of $Y$, Noetherian hypothesis, constructibility of $F$, invertibility of its torsion orders, or ground field is assumed.

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar y:P=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed and underlying point $y$, and put $T=X\times_Y P$ with projections $a:T\to P$ and $i:T\to X$. By proper base change of morphisms, $a$ is proper, hence of finite type by the definition of properness. Apply the fibre-dimension base-change lemma to $f$ and $\bar y$: for every $t\in T$, with image $x\in X_y$, $\dim_t T=\dim_x X_y$. The supremum-of-local-dimensions formula gives $\dim_t T\leq\dim X_y\leq d$, and then $\dim T\leq d$. This includes empty fibres, whose dimension is bottom. Thus $T$ is a finite-type $\Omega$-scheme of dimension at most $d$; no finiteness or Noetherian assumption on $Y$ has been used.

Let $G=i^{-1}F$. At a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$, the inverse-image stalk isomorphism identifies $G_{\bar t}$ with $F_{i\bar t}$. The latter is a torsion group by the torsion-sheaf characterization applied to $F$. Applying the converse characterization to $G$ proves that $G$ is a torsion abelian sheaf. This only requires elementwise torsion in each stalk, not one integer annihilating the whole sheaf.

source.place: Tag 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback), part (3), and Section 0DDB (torsion-sheaves), stalk characterization

proof.text: We first dispose of $T=\varnothing$. Every object of its small etale site is empty. The empty family of etale morphisms to an empty object is jointly surjective, hence is a covering by the definition of the small etale site. The abelian sheaf equalizer axiom therefore makes its section group zero (both products indexed by an empty set are the zero abelian group). For an injective resolution of $G$ the complex of global sections is consequently termwise zero, so $H^q(T,G)=0$ for every $q$.

source.place: Tag 095U (lemma-cohomological-dimension-proper), geometric-fibre reduction; empty-case expansion using the sheaf axiom

proof.text: For $T$ nonempty, put $e=\dim T$. Since $0\leq e\leq d$, $e$ is a finite nonnegative integer. Every irreducible polynomial over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$ has a root, hence is linear. Thus every element of a finite field extension of $\Omega$ has linear minimal polynomial and belongs to $\Omega$; in particular $\Omega$ has no nontrivial finite separable extension and is separably closed. Therefore the separably-closed-point vanishing lemma and the definition of torsion cohomological dimension give $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(\Omega)\leq0$. Apply the finite-type torsion cohomological dimension theorem with field $\Omega$, dimension exactly $e$, and $c=0$. It gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(T)\leq2e$. Unpacking the same definition for the torsion sheaf $G$ yields $H^q(T,G)=0$ whenever $q>2e$. In particular it vanishes for $q>2d$, because $2e\leq2d$.

source.place: Statement and proof; use c=0, with lem-kun-03qu-sep-closed.md; supplies the fibre vanishing required by Stacks 095U

proof.text: Apply bounded-below proper base change to the cartesian square with bottom map $\bar y$ and to $F[0]$. This complex has torsion cohomology and gives an isomorphism $\bar y^{-1}Rf_*F\cong Ra_*G$. Here inverse image is exact, so its degree-$q$ cohomology is $\bar y^{-1}R^qf_*F$. The global-sections functor $\Gamma(P,-)$ is exact and $\Gamma(P,\bar y^{-1}R^qf_*F)\cong(R^qf_*F)_{\bar y}$ by the geometric-point pullback lemma. To compute the other side, take a bounded-below injective resolution $G\to J^\bullet$. The definition of derived direct image represents $Ra_*G$ by $a_*J^\bullet$. Exactness of $\Gamma(P,-)$ lets it commute with cohomology (kernels and cokernels); the direct-image formula gives $\Gamma(P,a_*J^\bullet)=\Gamma(T,J^\bullet)$ term by term. By the definition of etale cohomology its degree-$q$ cohomology is $H^q(T,G)$. We have therefore derived $(R^qf_*F)_{\bar y}\cong H^q(T,G)$, which is zero for $q>2d$ by steps 3 and 4.

source.place: Tag 0DDF (lemma-proper-base-change-stalk), part (1), expanded from bounded-below proper base change and exact sections over a geometric point

proof.text: Fix $q>2d$. Step 5 applies to every geometric point of $Y$, and makes every stalk of $R^qf_*F$ the zero group. For the unique map $R^qf_*F\to0$ each geometric stalk map is thus an isomorphism. Geometric-stalk conservativity makes the sheaf map an isomorphism, proving $R^qf_*F=0$. When $Y$ is empty this same criterion is vacuous and still applies. The argument nowhere requires $Y$ quasi-compact, $F$ constructible, or any torsion order invertible.
